target_customer: Consumers, mainly teens and young adults on Meta Quest, plus licensing partners such as sports leagues
problem: Social VR needed a sports-first game that people actually want to play together; the company started as a social basketball game on Meta Quest and grew into a broader social games platform.
business_model: Free to play VR and mobile social platform monetized by in-app purchases, passes and league licensed content

founders.name: Justin Hubert
prior_employers: Insperience (Walmart Store No. 8), led VR art development
founders.background_notes: 3D artist specializing in VR production per YC page; company site also says he led art at his own VR game studio.

founders.name: Matthew Harris
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in the August 2022 funding coverage but not on the YC page; background not in the sources opened.

competitors.name: Rec Room
competitors.what: Free cross platform social VR space built around casual sports and party games such as dodgeball
competitors.traction_then: widely used social VR platform by 2018 per introduction article

technical_complexity.rationale: Multiplayer VR physics and netcode for a basketball game on standalone Quest hardware is hard for a small team but uses existing engines and the Meta platform.

defensibility.rationale: Game mechanics were copyable; the company later built league licenses with the NBA and MLB and a user community.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Meta controls the Quest platform; no source shows an incumbent copying Gym Class, and it added NBA (2023) and MLB (2025) licensing per YC.

market_need_then: Meta Quest 2 headset sales and social VR growth in 2021 and 2022 created a user base seeking multiplayer games; the demand evidence is the headset base, not a stated customer pain.

branding.domain_note: Uses gymclass.com, an exact match .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Sports and school gym themed social game

branding.brand_signature: The #gymclassvr hashtag and Meta Quest ratings (over 53K ratings, 4.8 stars per company site)
branding.community_and_virality: Company promotes #gymclassvr and active TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and X accounts; high Quest store ratings.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative school gym name fits the product and a large Quest ratings count suggests awareness, but no independent brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Gym Class began as a social basketball game on Meta Quest, raised an 8M seed from a16z in August 2022, and expanded to more sports, NBA and MLB licenses and a 2026 mobile launch. It is still active with about 20 people. Strong Quest ratings suggest product market fit, while dependence on the Meta platform and a small VR market remain the main risks. No later round was found.
notes: Company site says more than 8M raised, consistent with the seed; CB Insights shows 8.5M, unverified. Founding year differs: YC says 2021, SoCal Tech says 2019. Company site names CTO Erik (co-founder of tbh) without a surname; not listed. Competition search found no 2021 to 2022 sources naming rivals beyond Rec Room.
